title: Consent-aware soft-delete fanout and sampling harness for analytics retention
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Background: Console telemetry and usage analytics power product dashboards, billing heuristics, and model optimizations. We must support customer-driven consent/opt-out and per-attribute retention while preserving analytics signal for product teams. This ticket implements a consent-aware soft-delete fanout that emits privacy-safe sampled views to downstream consumers and produces verifiable deletion manifests for compliance teams. The harness will allow us to tune retention sampling ratios per dataset to reduce storage/cost while bounding statistical error for common queries.

Scope:
- Implement a soft-delete signal at the ingestion layer that marks events with deletion/consent flags and retains an immutable tombstone index.
- Build a fanout processor that reliably broadcasts deletion intents to downstream sinks (data lake, OLAP, export endpoints) with ordered retries and idempotency keys.
- Produce PRDs for sampled retention views: deterministic reservoir sampling keyed by customer and event type with configurable windowing.
- Add an auditable manifest generator (JSONL per run) that captures affected IDs, timestamps, and operator references for legal requests.
- Provide a rollout plan with canary (1% customers) and monitoring dashboards (missing-counts, downstream lag, SLO breach rate).

Non-goals: full crypto-shredding of all derived artifacts in this ticket (follow-up), global schema changes to telemetry payloads (minimal additions only).
acceptance_criteria: Soft-delete signal is emitted and persisted for >=99.9% of incoming events in staging
Fanout processor delivers deletion intents to S3/BigQuery exports and the analytics OLAP cluster with deduplication and at-least-once guarantees
Sampled retention views are generated with configurable sampling ratios and documented expected query error bounds
Audit manifests are produced and uploaded to the compliance bucket with validation checksums
Automated tests and a load test show <5% ingestion latency regression at peak traffic when the fanout is enabled
implementation_notes:
Component breakdown:
1) Ingest soft-delete flag: small schema extension (consent_version:int, soft_delete_ts:datetime, tombstone_ref:string). Backwards-compatible; default values for older clients.
2) Fanout processor: Kafka consumer -> idempotent dispatcher -> per-sink adapters (S3, BQ, Snowflake, webhook). Use monotonic sequence and last-applied map in Redis for dedupe.
3) Sampling harness: nightly batch that consumes tombstone index and rewrites sampled partitions; produces sample metadata (seed, algorithm, cardinality) to the metadata store.
4) Manifest generator: sign(manifest) with KMS HMAC key for tamper-evidence. Store signatures alongside manifests.

Trade-offs considered:
- Strong delete consistency (synchronous cross-sink delete) vs eventual fanout: chose eventual fanout with ordered retries to avoid end-to-end tail latency increases at ingest.
- Deterministic sampling vs reservoir sampling per window: deterministic keyed sampling preserves cohort stability across windows; reservoir sampling gives statistically optimal samples for fixed-size outputs. We will initially adopt deterministic keyed sampling with an option to switch for high-cardinality event types.
- Storage vs fidelity: sampled views reduce cost but increase query variance; teams must opt-in event types for sampling and provide baseline queries to compute error bounds.
comments: 2025-02-17 - Aisha Khan: Kickoff notes: aligned with Legal on manifest fields. Legal requested operator identity, original sink name, and request provenance in the manifest. Need to add KMS signing to scope.
2025-02-21 - Miguel Torres: Spike complete for idempotent dispatcher. Redis-based last-applied map works for our scale in perf tests. Draft PR opened (see design links).

2025-02-24 - Priya Desai (Product): PM feedback: product analytics teams expressed concern about baseline query accuracy on sampled views; requested a verifier job that computes sample error for a set of canonical queries. Adding to acceptance criteria.
2025-02-27 - Security review note: Security team flagged KMS HMAC key rotation requirements and RBAC around manifest access. Marking security_review_required = true and scheduling review meeting.

2025-03-01 - Miguel Torres: Load test results: with fanout enabled we see 3.8% p95 ingestion latency increase at peak (acceptable). Fanout queue backed up at 10x baseline for 12 minutes during simulated downstream outage; we need a throttling/backpressure policy and alerting (pager duty).

2025-03-03 - Aisha Khan: Updated acceptance criteria with target manifest checksum validation and added dashboard widgets (fanout success rate, downstream lag, manifests-signed-per-hour). Next: implement verifier job and add canary rollout scripts.
notes_for_ops: Rollout: feature flag gated by customer. Start with internal customers only, then 1% canary, 10% ramp, full rollout. Ops runbook: if fanout queue >24h backlog, escalate to infra and flip feature flag to disable fanout but preserve tombstone writes. Manifest retention: keep for 7 years in compliance bucket.
qa_plan: Unit tests for dispatcher and dedupe; integration tests with a local S3 emulator and BigQuery emulator; synthetic dataset with ground-truth deletions to validate manifests and sampling error estimator; performance test at 2x expected daily volume.
risks: Risk: downstream consumers that rely on full-fidelity data may break if sampling is applied without coordination. Mitigation: opt-in per-event-type and notify owner teams. Risk: manifest leak — restrict access via IAM and audit logs.
next_steps: Finalize manifest schema with Legal and Security
Complete PR for idempotent dispatcher and land adapters for S3 and BQ
Build verifier job to compute sample error for canonical queries
